transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Mehta (CISO, Argon), Omar Ruiz (Head of Cloud Platform), Renee Park (Legal), Benji Kaur (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick readout on Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO posture, how Argon can access evidence in the Trust Center, and alignment on data residency/KMS needs for a potential Private deployment pilot. Agreed to share redacted reports and schedule RBAC deep dive.

Topics covered:
- Trust Center access and evidence delivery mechanics
- SOC 2 Type II scope and ISO 27001 certification status
- RBAC/SSO (SAML/SCIM) mapping and provisioning flow
- Audit logs: retention, export, and format (JSON/CSV)
- Encryption at rest and BYOK/KMS/HSM options
- Data residency and EU region benchmarks / private deployment tradeoffs

00:00:05 Ethan Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Ethan from Redwood, i'll kick off. we got Priya from SE here too. quick round of intros?
00:00:18 Laura Mehta: Hi, Laura here, CISO at Argon Therapeutics. we're mostly focused on the compliance posture — SOC2 + ISO 27001 alignment — and evidence access patterns.
00:00:27 Priya Nair: thanks Laura, hi all. i'm Priya, i work on deployment and security integrations. we'll try to address RBAC, SSO, logs and key management today.
00:00:39 Omar Ruiz: Omar — cloud lead. main constraints: EU data residency, 12-month audit log retention, and our IdP is Okta.
00:00:47 Benji Kaur: Benji, DevOps — i'll be hands on for any test credentials, infra, et cetera.
00:00:53 Renee Park: Renee, legal — will be looking for contractual guarantees around data residency and evidence access windows.

00:01:12 Ethan Cole: Great. high level — Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. we give customers read access to the Trust Center where redacted artifacts live. we'll share the redacted Type II today as a follow up. quick question for Argon: are you ok with redacted reports, or do you need unredacted artifacts under NDA?
00:01:35 Laura Mehta: For initial evaluation redacted is fine. but for our audit we might need specific evidence exports later, under NDA.
00:01:43 Ethan Cole: Totally expected. we'll follow a staged approach: redacted artifacts then, if needed, a controlled evidence pull under NDA and scoped access.
00:01:51 Priya Nair: On the Trust Center — it's a web portal with export capabilities. we provide links, PDF reports, and common evidence bundles (config snapshots, runbooks, SOC control descriptions). there is also an API to pull artifacts programmatically if you need automation.
00:02:16 Omar Ruiz: Can you confirm audit log formats? we need structured logs for SIEM ingestion — ideally JSON with timestamp and request metadata.
00:02:24 Priya Nair: logs are JSON lines by default, with request id, timestamp, model id, route, and outcome. retention is 90 days for hosted by default; for enterprise/dedicated you can get 12 months retention or export hooks to your S3.
00:02:41 Laura Mehta: 90 days is not enough for us. we need 12 months and an option to push to our EU S3 bucket.
00:02:47 Priya Nair: understood — for Dedicated or Private deployments we support configurable retention and S3 sink, including cross-region endpoints for EU. note there are costs and throughput implications.
00:02:59 Ethan Cole: sounds like Dedicated or Private is the direction if you need long retention and strict residency.

00:03:20 Omar Ruiz: can we discuss KMS? we have a BYOK requirement in some contracts. does Redwood support customer-managed keys / HSM?
00:03:27 Priya Nair: yes, we support BYOK for Private deployments and dedicated with an enterprise KMS integration. we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSMs in on-prem packages. some customers want HSM-backed key wrapping for KV cache encryption, which is supported in the private runtime.
00:03:46 Benji Kaur: sorry, you said KV cache — did you mean K V cache? can we get clarification on what is encrypted?
00:03:53 Priya Nair: yeah, bad transcription in the portal sometimes. we encrypt the model KV cache at rest, request logs, and customer payloads using envelope encryption. the data plane uses TLS in transit and envelope encryption at rest; keys are wrapped with your KMS key if BYOK is enabled.

00:04:20 Renee Park: from legal: if we go down the private route we need proof you won't have access to unencrypted customer payloads when BYOK is used.
00:04:29 Priya Nair: with BYOK + HSM, Redwood doesn't have key material. we can provide architecture diagrams and a key custody statement. we'll add that to the Trust Center pack.

00:04:50 Ethan Cole: quick note on SSO and RBAC: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups and roles. typical flow is: your IdP (Okta) syncs groups via SCIM to Redwood, and we map groups to RBAC roles which control console and Trust Center access.
00:05:08 Laura Mehta: great. we want least privilege by default. can we map auditors to read-only Trust Center roles?
00:05:14 Priya Nair: yes, there are built-in roles: admin, dev, viewer, auditor. auditor has read-only access to Trust Center artifacts and logs exports.
00:05:23 Omar Ruiz: for provisioning we may want to limit group sync to a subset; do you allow scoping of SCIM to specific group OUs?
00:05:30 Priya Nair: Yes, SCIM supports group filters; you can control which groups are synced and which roles they map to. sometimes customers create an 'redwood-audit' group and only sync that.

00:05:50 Laura Mehta: can you talk about the control mapping? our audit team will need a point-by-point mapping to our SOC 2 controls and ISO clauses.
00:05:58 Priya Nair: we maintain a control mapping matrix (excel) that maps our internal controls to common frameworks. we'll populate it with which artifacts are available in Trust Center. for items not covered by Redwood (e.g., customer-side patching) we'll mark as customer responsibility.
00:06:16 Ethan Cole: we'll share that mapping as part of the follow-up. Priya, action on control mapping?
00:06:21 Priya Nair: yes, I'll prepare a matrix with sample evidence pull steps and examples of artifacts (config snapshots, SOC control test evidence, rotation logs).

00:06:35 Renee Park: for evidence export, what's the process to get unredacted files under NDA?
00:06:40 Ethan Cole: two options: 1) a scheduled evidence pull we run with an NDA and scoped access; or 2) we provision a private, controlled view for named users to access raw artifacts for a limited window. which do you prefer?
00:06:54 Renee Park: legal prefers we see the raw artifacts ourselves under NDA first.
00:06:58 Ethan Cole: ok we'll prepare an NDA template and a process doc.

00:07:10 Omar Ruiz: any hard network requirements? we prefer to run Private in our VPC or see a VPC peering option.
00:07:17 Priya Nair: Private deployment can be run in your VPC (customer-managed) or as a managed VPC with strict network controls. we can provide an air-gapped on-prem bundle if needed for higher-regulated workloads.
00:07:30 Benji Kaur: how long to stand up a private instance for a pilot?
00:07:34 Priya Nair: for a minimal pilot typically 2-4 weeks for provisioning and validation — depends on region and hardware lead times.

00:07:50 Laura Mehta: are there any public pen test summaries or third-party assessments?
00:07:55 Ethan Cole: yes, we have pen test summaries and the third-party assessor report is in the Trust Center. redacted executive summaries are shareable and we'll attach the assessor's contact under NDA.

00:08:10 Omar Ruiz: on the EU benchmark, would you be able to run a latency/cost test from eu-west-1 with our sample workload? we want to see 99th percentile latency and cost per token.
00:08:20 Priya Nair: we can run a targeted benchmark in eu-west-1; we'll need a small workload sample and test credentials. We can also show the difference between hosted vs dedicated vs private in the same region.
00:08:33 Ethan Cole: we'll set that up as a SE-led job. target window — next week.

00:08:45 Benji Kaur: one practical question — for log export to our EU S3, do you support server-side encryption with our KMS key?
00:08:53 Priya Nair: yes, S3 sink supports SSE-KMS with your key and cross-account roles. we'll include the role trust policy example in the doc.

00:09:05 Renee Park: contractual note — we need to ensure that audit rights and evidence access are spelled out in the Master Services Agreement.
00:09:12 Ethan Cole: absolutely, we'll surface the standard clause and we can work with legal on redlines.

00:09:25 (brief cross talk / hold music)

00:10:00 Priya Nair: demoing the Trust Center briefly — (screen share) — top-level page shows certifications, then a control-by-control index. you can search by control id, or export a bundle. there's an artifacts api we can call with a token.
00:10:20 Laura Mehta: is that api access restricted by role? we don't want auditors to get more than they should.
00:10:25 Priya Nair: yes, token scopes are role-bound. auditor tokens can only list and download redacted artifacts unless the account owner grants expanded scope.

00:10:45 Omar Ruiz: about identity lifecycle, how do you handle deprovisioning?
00:10:50 Priya Nair: deprovisioning is immediate when SCIM removes a user; sessions are revoked and access tokens expire. we also publish an activity log of user provisioning actions to the audit log.

00:11:06 Laura Mehta: retention of SSO audit logs — we need 12 months. can you keep auth logs for that period?
00:11:12 Priya Nair: yes in Dedicated/Private you can configure auth log retention up to 24 months. hosted has default shorter windows.

00:11:25 Ethan Cole: any blockers or must-have items to decide next week?
00:11:30 Laura Mehta: must-haves: BYOK with HSM proof, 12-month log retention in EU, and contractual language on evidence access.
00:11:37 Renee Park: also need to see a control mapping matrix.

00:11:45 Priya Nair: we'll provide: 1) redacted SOC 2 Type II report, 2) ISO scope and certificate, 3) control mapping matrix, 4) Trust Center link and API docs, 5) NDA template for evidence pulls.

00:12:05 Ethan Cole: ok let's talk timeline: we'll share docs by Friday (2026-06-20). Priya will kick off the EU benchmark as soon as Argon hands over a small workload sample and creds.

00:12:18 Omar Ruiz: one more question on encryption in transit — any custom ciphers or is it standard TLS 1.3?
00:12:23 Priya Nair: standard TLS 1.3. we can provide cipher suites and cert chain info in the security pack.

00:12:35 Benji Kaur: can you put together a short runbook for incident response — our SOC wants to know how to request logs in a breach scenario.
00:12:42 Priya Nair: yes, we'll add an IR playbook excerpt.

00:12:50 (background noise)

00:13:05 Ethan Cole: cool, we'll mark the action items in the follow-up email. any final questions?
00:13:12 Laura Mehta: just one — does Redwood support region-specific contracts for data residency (e.g., EU-only data processing clause)?
00:13:21 Ethan Cole: Yes, we have addenda for data processing that can restrict processing to EU regions and specify personnel access limits. we'll surface a sample addendum.
00:13:33 Renee Park: thanks. legal will review the sample addendum and come back with redlines.

00:13:40 Priya Nair: i'll follow up on the SCIM mapping details and the sample role mappings.
00:13:46 Ethan Cole: we'll send the initial packet by Friday. I'll also include pricing options for Dedicated vs Private so you can weigh cost vs control.

00:13:58 Omar Ruiz: quick FYI — our procurement window is end of July, so would like to have the pilot up before mid-July.
00:14:06 Ethan Cole: noted, we'll try to prioritize the pilot schedule to hit that window.

00:14:15 (meeting wrap; 1:1 side conversation omitted)

00:14:30 Transcript notes / imperfections: occasional word swap (K V case / KV cache), nicknames, and a few truncated words due to cross talk; some proper nouns might be auto-corrected by the transcription engine.

End of recording.
